records.text:
Laboratory Tests:
- Baseline blood tests were normal, including lipid and serum iron levels
- Hypocomplementemic state noted (C3: 65 mg/dL, C4: 8 mg/dL, C1q: <29 mg/L)
- Immunoglobulin G–κ type monoclonal gammopathy (1120 mg/dL on serum protein electrophoresis)
- Urinalysis negative for Bence Jones protein
- Bone marrow biopsy findings were normal

Imaging Studies:
Radiologic imaging showed no visceral or osseous involvement

Pathology:
Skin Biopsies:
First biopsy: granulomatous folliculitis with scarlike fibrosis
Subsequent biopsies showed:
- Diffuse fibrosis with scarlike morphologic features
- Vessels aligned perpendicularly within extensive fibrosis parallel to epidermis
- Prominent infiltrate of CD68+ histiocytes interspersed with multinucleated cells
- Some cells similar to Touton giant cells
- Perls iron stain showed red blood cell extravasation and marked hemosiderin deposition
- Verhoeff staining showed elastic fibers palisading under the dermal nodule
Initial choroidal biopsy: granulomatous reaction with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate

Images:
Figure 1: Several firm mahogany-brown papules and linear plaques, showing arborizing pattern and resembling keloids, located on trunk and extensor knees
Figure 2: Histologic findings showing deep cicatricial fibrosis, multinucleate cells, and Perls iron stain demonstrating erythrocyte extravasation

bindings.label: Bilateral conjunctival erythema and asymptomatic skin lesions on the lower limbs, trunk, and upper limbs

65-year-old man with medical history of coronary artery disease, treated dyslipidemia, and hypertension; initial ophthalmology presentation showed bilateral conjunctival erythema and choroidal thickening

One year after initial presentation, asymptomatic skin lesions appeared on lower limbs and progressed to trunk and upper limbs; a 3-week tapered course of oral prednisone (60 mg/d) showed no improvement; physical examination revealed many flat, firm, brownish papules and plaques resembling keloids, some linear with an arborizing pattern, symmetrically involving lower limbs, trunk, and upper limbs while sparing face, oral mucosa, and flexor regions
One year later, immunoglobulin G–κ type monoclonal gammopathy developed
Skin biopsy shows deep fibrosis with CD68+ histiocytes, Touton-like giant cells, and hemosiderin deposition
Skin biopsy shows no mucin deposition
Mucin special stains and thyroid function test results are missing
Bone marrow examination shows normal findings
Bence Jones protein test is negative
Scleromyxedema with positive mucin special stain (mucinosis confirmed)
Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma with negative mucin special stain (histiocytic disorder confirmed)
Serum tryptase was elevated at 42 ng/mL and the bone marrow aspirate showed mast cell infiltration
